c.v: Should a 20 year old roof be replaced?

runs.v: Often, but age alone does not decide it. A 3-tab asphalt roof reaches the end of its rated 20-year life at that age, while an architectural roof rated for about 30 years may have useful years left, per the InterNACHI chart. A professional evaluates a roof's condition to determine necessary repairs or replacement, and the roof's integrity decides the call. Common roof issues include leaks and missing shingles, and when missing shingles, curling or cracked tabs, granule loss, soft decking, and repeated active leaks show up together, they point to a full roof replacement, while minor repairs make sense on a sound deck.

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: Roofers use a rule of thumb that once damage covers more than about 25% of a roof, a full replacement usually costs less in the long run than continued repairs, and New Jersey's code draws a similar line for permits on commercial, multi-family, and attached buildings under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. Orange homeowners and property managers of multi-family properties can book free roof inspections to get the answer in writing, with photographs, before spending on either path. When replacement wins, roof replacement projects should ideally be scheduled during milder seasons to prevent installation issues, since spring and fall temperatures let shingles seal and adhesives cure.

runs.v: A crew sizes ventilation against the NRCA and ARMA standard of 1 square foot of net-free vent area per 150 square feet of attic floor and checks whether the property needs historic-district review before any material change. sections.heading: How to Choose Orange Roofing Contractors for a Roof Replacement

runs.v: Every company calls itself a premier roofing contractor, so check the proof instead. Any residential roofing contractor in New Jersey must be registered as a Home Improvement Contractor, and the state issues no separate roofing license, so a roofer advertising as "fully licensed" should be able to show that registration. New Jersey requires home improvement contractors to carry general liability insurance, and contractors with employees must carry workers' compensation coverage, so ask for proof of both and a written estimate that details materials, labor, disposal, and the schedule. Per New Jersey law, homeowners can cancel a home improvement contract within three business days of signing. Ask neighbors who replaced a roof recently how the crews handled cleanup, gutters, siding, and skylights, and whether the job finished on schedule.
